# core/endian.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/endian.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Fixed-width integers stored in byte strings, as
packet headers, file formats and disk blocks hold them.

What is proved: every access is in bounds; the 16-bit loads and stores
also state their value in terms of the two bytes.

`import "core/endian.bastio";`

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`load_le16`](#load_le16) | The little-endian `u16` at `b[at..at+2]`. |
| [`load_be16`](#load_be16) | The big-endian `u16` at `b[at..at+2]` (network byte order). |
| [`load_le32`](#load_le32) | The little-endian `u32` at `b[at..at+4]`. |
| [`load_be32`](#load_be32) | The big-endian `u32` at `b[at..at+4]`. |
| [`load_le64`](#load_le64) | The little-endian `u64` at `b[at..at+8]`. |
| [`load_be64`](#load_be64) | The big-endian `u64` at `b[at..at+8]`. |
| [`store_le16`](#store_le16) | Stores `v` little-endian at `b[at..at+2]`. |
| [`store_be16`](#store_be16) | Stores `v` big-endian at `b[at..at+2]` (network byte order). |
| [`store_le32`](#store_le32) | Stores `v` little-endian at `b[at..at+4]`. |
| [`store_be32`](#store_be32) | Stores `v` big-endian at `b[at..at+4]` (network byte order). |
| [`store_le64`](#store_le64) | Stores `v` little-endian at `b[at..at+8]`. |
| [`store_be64`](#store_be64) | Stores `v` big-endian at `b[at..at+8]` (network byte order). |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `load_le16`

```bastio
fn load_le16(b: &Bytes, at: u64) -> u16
  requires at + 2 <= blen(b)
  ensures result == bget(b, at) + 256 * bget(b, at + 1)
```

The little-endian `u16` at `b[at..at+2]`.

Example:

```bastio
let mut b = balloc(8);
store_be16(&mut b, 0, 4660);   // 0x1234, network byte order
let x = load_be16(b, 0);
assert x == 4660;              // the 16-bit contracts state the bytes
let y = load_le16(b, 0);       // the same bytes read the other way
bfree(b);
if y != 13330 { return 1; }    // 0x3412
```

### `load_be16`

```bastio
fn load_be16(b: &Bytes, at: u64) -> u16
  requires at + 2 <= blen(b)
  ensures result == 256 * bget(b, at) + bget(b, at + 1)
```

The big-endian `u16` at `b[at..at+2]` (network byte order).

### `load_le32`

```bastio
fn load_le32(b: &Bytes, at: u64) -> u32
  requires at + 4 <= blen(b)
```

The little-endian `u32` at `b[at..at+4]`.

Example:

```bastio
let mut b = balloc(8);
store_le32(&mut b, 0, 305419896);   // 0x12345678
let x = load_le32(b, 0);
let y = load_be32(b, 0);
store_be32(&mut b, 4, 1);
let z = bget(b, 7);
bfree(b);
if x != 305419896 || y != 2018915346 || z != 1 { return 1; }
```

### `load_be32`

```bastio
fn load_be32(b: &Bytes, at: u64) -> u32
  requires at + 4 <= blen(b)
```

The big-endian `u32` at `b[at..at+4]`.

### `load_le64`

```bastio
fn load_le64(b: &Bytes, at: u64) -> u64
  requires at + 8 <= blen(b)
```

The little-endian `u64` at `b[at..at+8]`.

Example:

```bastio
let mut b = balloc(16);
store_be64(&mut b, 0, 1);
store_le64(&mut b, 8, 1);
let x = load_le64(b, 0);   // 1 << 56
let y = load_be64(b, 0);
let z = load_le64(b, 8);
store_le16(&mut b, 0, 65535);
let w = load_be16(b, 0);
bfree(b);
if x != 72057594037927936 || y != 1 || z != 1 || w != 65535 { return 1; }
```

### `load_be64`

```bastio
fn load_be64(b: &Bytes, at: u64) -> u64
  requires at + 8 <= blen(b)
```

The big-endian `u64` at `b[at..at+8]`.

### `store_le16`

```bastio
fn store_le16(b: &mut Bytes, at: u64, v: u16)
  requires at + 2 <= blen(b)
  ensures blen(b) == blen(old(b))
  ensures bget(b, at) + 256 * bget(b, at + 1) == v
```

Stores `v` little-endian at `b[at..at+2]`.

### `store_be16`

```bastio
fn store_be16(b: &mut Bytes, at: u64, v: u16)
  requires at + 2 <= blen(b)
  ensures blen(b) == blen(old(b))
  ensures 256 * bget(b, at) + bget(b, at + 1) == v
```

Stores `v` big-endian at `b[at..at+2]` (network byte order).
